lines: A copy of ALM's Beast's Chalkboard: two precision adders, each passing its input straight through and offering two copies with a whole number of volts added
Adds a whole number of volts to the first section's pair of Out jacks, -2V to +2V in one-volt steps, and nothing at the centre
Adds a whole number of volts to the second section's pair of Out jacks, -2V to +2V in one-volt steps, and nothing at the centre
The signal the first section passes and adds to; it is also what the second section reads when nothing is patched there
The signal the second section passes and adds to; with nothing patched it takes the first section's input
The first input passed through with nothing added to it
The first input with the first switch's offset added
The second input passed through with nothing added to it
The second input with the second switch's offset added
Note — both switches come up at the centre, adding nothing, so out of the box the Out jacks carry exactly what the Thru jacks carry.
Note — nothing is clamped anywhere. The offset is added to whatever arrives, so a large input can be pushed past the range other modules expect.
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.

Beast.notes:
There is no published source for this plugin: plugin.json carries no sourceUrl and no manualUrl, so everything here was read out of the installed 2.2.2 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped and carries one Class::process per model.

The switch is a five-position rotary: configParam at 0x269c and 0x2714 gives -2 to +2 in the unit V with snapEnabled set at 0x26e4, and the panel prints -2, -I, a zero symbol, +I and +2 around it. process adds that number of volts, so the module is an octave shifter when it is fed a 1V-per-octave pitch, which is what it is for.

The normal runs from the first section to the second, not the other way: process reads input 1's channel count and falls back to input 0. The panel prints a down-pointing triangle beside both In jacks, which on the second one points at nothing.

Both Out jacks of a section are written from the same value, so they are exact duplicates and share a line.

This model registers no context menu: nm shows appendContextMenu on the OAx2, Tangle, MCO, MFD, MegaTang and PipSlope widgets only.

lines: A copy of ALM's O/A/x2: two channels, each multiplying its input by an attenuverter and adding a fixed voltage to the result
Adds a fixed voltage to the first channel, -10V to +10V, and comes up at the centre where it adds nothing
Scales the first channel's input between -2 and +2, silent at the centre of its travel and inverting below it; it comes up at the centre
Adds a fixed voltage to the second channel, -10V to +10V, and comes up at the centre where it adds nothing
Scales the second channel's input between -2 and +2, silent at the centre of its travel and inverting below it; it comes up at the centre
The signal the first channel scales; with nothing patched the channel puts out its offset alone
The signal the second channel scales; with nothing patched the channel puts out its offset alone
The first channel's input times its attenuverter plus its offset, clamped to ±12V
The second channel's input times its attenuverter plus its offset, clamped to ±12V; with MIX MODE on the first channel's result is added here too, unless a cable is in the first channel's output
Note — both attenuverters come up at the centre, where they pass nothing at all. A fresh module puts out only what the two offset knobs are set to, which is 0V.
Note — the two lamps beside each output show the sign of that output, one for voltage above 0V and one for below, reaching full at 10V.
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Menu — MIX MODE — adds the first channel's result into the second channel's output; the addition stops while a cable is in the first channel's own output jack

OAx2.notes:
No family is set on these jacks. The module is a DC-coupled offset and attenuverter pair; what a jack carries is whatever you decide to put in it, so a colour would be a guess.

The mix is a menu item, not a knob. Param 4 is configured (0x11c3c, 0 to 1, default 0) but no ParamWidget is created for it, so it has no position in the census and cannot be clicked for help; OAx2Widget::appendContextMenu at 0x12568 builds it with createBoolMenuItem under the name assembled inline at 0x125dc, which is MIX MODE in capitals.

The mix is also conditional in a way the name does not suggest: 0x11f14-0x11f24 reads output 0's channel count and contributes -0.0 instead of the first channel's value when that output is patched. Plug anything into the first channel's output and the second channel stops receiving it.

The attenuverter reaches ±2, so the module amplifies as well as attenuates. Both attenuverters default to 0, which is the middle of their travel and passes nothing.

Four lights are driven from the two results at 0x11f78-0x11fb8 and 0x12008-0x12048, scaled by 0.1 so they reach full at 10V, with a separate lamp for each sign.

The signal that channel amplifies
Sets that channel's level, 0V for silence and the top of the chosen voltage range for the knob's full setting; a cable sitting at 0V therefore silences the channel
That channel's signal after its level; putting a cable in here takes the channel out of the Mix
The sum of those channels whose own output jacks are empty
Note — a channel leaves the Mix the moment a cable goes into its own output jack. That is how one module is split between a mix and separate destinations.
Note — nothing here is clamped. A level CV above the chosen voltage range drives the channel past unity gain.
Note — the lamp beside each channel follows that channel's level setting rather than the signal passing through it.
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Menu — Voltage Range: 10V, 5V — sets the voltage the four Level CV jacks treat as a channel's full level

Tangle.notes:
This is the plainest example in the plugin of a CV input that takes the knob over rather than adding to it. Tangle::process at 0x17f3c-0x17f50 computes gain = CV * knob / range when the Level CV jack is patched, and gain = knob when it is not. A patched cable resting at 0V silences the channel however far up the knob is, and the knob becomes an attenuator for the CV.

The four channels are written from the same shape of code and differ only in which port and which knob they use, so one line covers each role and the tags point all four at it.

The Mix jack is a normalled sum: 0x18048-0x18060 and 0x1807c-0x1808c read each channel output's channel count and drop that channel from the total when it is patched. The maker's own product page for the hardware describes the same behaviour.

The level knobs are configured 0 to 1 with a default of 1 and a display multiplier of 100 (0x17974-0x17998), so they are percentages and come up fully open. The lights are fed the gain value, not the audio.

The menu name is the literal string "Voltage Range" at 0x188b0, with the two choices assembled inline at 0x188d0 and 0x188e4 as 10V and 5V. The getter at 0x18ba0 compares the stored range against 5 and the setter at 0x18c98 stores 10 for index 0 and 5 for index 1, so 10V is the first choice and the one a new module has (set at 0x17054).

lines: A copy of ALM's MCO: a digital wavetable oscillator giving a sub square, a gated pulse and the main wave at the same time
Sets the pitch over five and a half octaves: the frequency is 165Hz multiplied by two to the power of this setting, and then by the fine trim
Multiplies the frequency by between 1 and 2, which is one octave across its travel; it comes up in the middle at 1.5
Chooses which wave is read out of the table, from the start of the table to the end of it; it comes up at the start
Sets the width of the Pulse output across its whole range; it comes up at nothing
Sets the pitch at one volt per octave, multiplying the frequency by two to the power of the voltage
Moves the choice of wave, adding to the knob, with the voltage range chosen on the menu covering the knob's whole travel
Moves the pulse width, adding to the knob, with the voltage range chosen on the menu covering the knob's whole travel
Sets how many times the pulse pattern repeats inside one cycle of the wave, one to four across the chosen voltage range; there is no knob for this, so with nothing patched it stays at one
Restarts the wave from the beginning of the table whenever the voltage rises past 1V, and flips the sub square at the same moment
A square wave one octave below the pitch, swinging between -7V and 7V, which flips at the end of every cycle
The wave gated into a pulse: 7V wherever the phase falls outside the width set by the PWM control, and the wave itself inside it
The wave read out of the table at the set pitch, reaching ±7V at full scale
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Note — a new module runs near 247Hz. The frequency is 165Hz times two to the power of the coarse setting, times the fine trim.
Menu — Input CV Range: 10V, 5V — sets the voltage the Wave, PWM and Type inputs treat as a full sweep of their control

2.why: plugin.dylib MCO::process 0x5d08-0x5d20 writes the wave sample scaled by 7/32767 to one channel

MCO.notes:
Parameter 3, the Type control, exists but has no knob and no configParam. MCO::MCO calls configParam for indices 0, 1, 2 and 4 only (0x562c, 0x5690, 0x5700, 0x5770); index 3 keeps the empty default quantity that Module::config creates, which is why the census records it with no name and no position. combine_cv_and_pot_data never reads params[3] either — only the Type jack, divided by the voltage range and clamped to that default 0 to 1. So the Type jack has no knob behind it at all and is the only way to change that setting. It gets no tag, because no click can reach the parameter.

A second dead computation sits at 0x61cc-0x6268: the fine-tune parameter is combined with the Sync jack's voltage as though that jack were a CV, clamped, and stored at +0x178. Nothing reads +0x178. The Sync jack's real use is the level comparison in process at 0x5c64. The fine trim therefore has no CV input.

The frequency law is 165 * 2^coarse * fine. configParam at 0x5770 gives the coarse control -2.75 to 2.75 with a display base of 2 and a display multiplier of 165, and 0x5700 gives the fine control 1 to 2 with a default of 1.5. Both use MCO::FreqParamQuantity, whose getDisplayValueString reads a frequency the process code stores back into it, so the tooltips show hertz.

Outputs are scaled by 7/32767 (the constant 0x396001C0 at 0x5cf4), so a full-scale sample leaves at 7V and the sub square is a hard ±7V.

The pulse output is not a plain square. 0x5cb0-0x5ce8 divides the cycle into as many parts as the Type setting asks for, compares the position inside the current part against the pulse width, and outputs a flat 7V outside it and the wave itself inside it. With Type at one and the width at zero the jack sits at 7V.

The maker's product page for the hardware describes "Voltage control of frequency, waveshape, pulse width and distribution" and "3 Outputs; wavetable, PWM'd wavetable & sub", which matches; it quotes no figures, so none were taken from it.

lines: A copy of ALM's Pip Slope Mk2: a digital attack-and-decay envelope with a variable curve and three ways of repeating itself
Sets the attack time, shortest at the bottom of its travel and longest at the top; it comes up in the middle
Sets the decay time, shortest at the bottom of its travel and longest at the top; it comes up in the middle
Bends the curve of both stages, with one shape below the middle of its travel and its mirror image above; it comes up in the middle

Chooses how the envelope repeats: one shot at the bottom of its travel, then a band that repeats with the level halving, then a band of four to ten shortening repeats, and an endless loop near the top
Starts the envelope from zero whenever the voltage rises past 3V
Starts the envelope on a rise past 3V and then holds it at the top of the attack for as long as the voltage stays above 3V, letting the decay run once it falls
Lengthens the attack, adding to the knob; the top of the chosen voltage range adds about three quarters of the knob's own range, and negative voltage does nothing
Lengthens the decay, adding to the knob; the top of the chosen voltage range adds about three quarters of the knob's own range, and negative voltage does nothing
A pulse at the top of the chosen voltage range, 100 samples long, at the end of every envelope
The envelope, from 0V to the top of the chosen voltage range; the menu here offers 10V or 5V where the hardware offers 8V or 5V
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Note — nothing happens until something triggers it. Patch a rising voltage above 3V into Trig or Gate, or turn the Loop control past about a quarter of its travel so that the envelope drives itself.
Note — one lamp follows the envelope level; a second lights while the Loop control is in its endless band.
Menu — Voltage Range: 10V, 5V — sets how high the Slope Out and the End of Slope pulse reach, and the voltage the two CV inputs treat as a full sweep

2.why: plugin.dylib PipSlope::ManageHardware 0x14630-0x1467c skips the store when the voltage is below zero, and otherwise scales it by 767 divided by the voltage-range member; MillisecondCallback 0x14ad4-0x14af8 multiplies that by four and adds it to the knob's own 0 to 4094 value

3.why: plugin.dylib PipSlope::ManageHardware 0x14640-0x146a8 and MillisecondCallback 0x14afc-0x14b18, the same arrangement as the attack CV, for the decay

0.why: plugin.dylib PipSlope::slope_yield 0x14a9c-0x14ac0 writes the voltage-range member for a countdown of 100 passes and then zero, one channel

1.why: plugin.dylib PipSlope::process 0x1458c-0x145b0 scales the 12-bit envelope by the voltage-range member divided by 4095.5 and writes one channel

PipSlope.notes:
The code and ALM's own hardware page disagree about the output level. The page for the ALM028 says "Selectable 5v or 8v max envelope level output"; the menu here (built at 0x15130, name "Voltage Range", choices assembled inline at 0x151c8 and 0x151dc) offers 10V and 5V, and the setter stores 10 or 5 into the same member the output scaling reads. The Slope Out line carries that clause; a patch built around the hardware's 8V will be a third too loud here at the default setting.

The Loop control's bands come from MillisecondCallback at 0x14b2c-0x14c18, which reads the knob as a 0 to 4095 number and picks a mode: below 1001 one shot, 1001 and above a mode that halves the peak each repeat (slope_yield 0x149b4), 2001 and above a mode that runs four to ten repeats at shortening rates taken from a table (0x149e0 and 0x148cc), and 3401 and above a mode that retriggers itself every millisecond, which also lights a lamp at 0x14b48. ALM's page describes the hardware's three loop modes as "Decreasing amplitude, decreasing time, and regular loop", which is the same set.

The Gate input really does sustain. ManageHardware records only its rising edge, but slope_yield reads the jack's level directly at 0x14918 and freezes the envelope while it is above 3V.

The knobs are read as 12-bit numbers exactly as the hardware's firmware would see them: ManageHardware at 0x145dc scales each 0-to-1 parameter by 4095.5 and offsets the two time controls by 8191.5, and MillisecondCallback subtracts 8190 and clamps to 0..4094. The lamp at 0x14b4c is set to a brightness of 2, which Rack clamps to full.

Every figure here was read out of the binary. Nothing was taken from the hardware manual PDF, which was not opened.

lines: A copy of ALM's MEGA-TANG: four channels with level, pan, mute and an effects send, summed into a stereo mix, with a stereo return and two optional expanders
Sets how much of that channel reaches the Send output, taken after its level and its mute; it comes up at nothing
Places that channel between the left and right mix outputs and comes up at the centre
Sets that channel's level from silence to unity and comes up fully open; while that channel's Levels CV jack is patched the knob stops setting the level and scales the jack's voltage instead
Silences that channel in the stereo mix and in the send; the channel's own output jack goes on carrying it at full level
The signal that channel mixes
Sets that channel's level, 0V for silence and the top of the chosen voltage range for the knob's full setting; a cable sitting at 0V therefore silences the channel
The left side of the effects return, added straight into the left mix output; nothing is copied to the right side, despite the (m) printed on the panel
The right side of the effects return, added straight into the right mix output
That channel's signal after its level, with the mute ignored; putting a cable in here takes the channel out of the stereo mix and out of the send
The left side of the mix: every channel whose own output is empty, at its panned level, plus the left return
The right side of the mix: every channel whose own output is empty, at its panned level, plus the right return
The four channels at their send settings, after their levels and mutes, added together
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Note — the four send knobs come up at nothing, so the Send output is silent until one is raised. The level knobs come up fully open and the pans at the centre.
Note — a mute takes effect on the sample it is pressed, with no fade. ALM's page for the hardware describes soft-close mutes that avoid clicks; there is no smoothing in this port.
Note — MT-EX1 and MT-EX2 attach immediately to the right of this module. Either one is inert anywhere else.
Note — with an MT-EX1 attached, this module writes a line of debug text to standard output on every audio sample. It changes nothing about the sound but fills a log quickly.
Menu — Voltage Range: 10V, 5V — sets the voltage the four Levels CV jacks treat as a channel's full level

6.why: plugin.dylib MegaTang::process 0xf9f0 writes the send total to one channel with no clamp

MegaTang.notes:
The return is not mono-normalled. The panel prints (m) beside the left Return jack, which is ALM's mark for a jack that feeds both sides when used alone, and MFD in this same plugin does exactly that. MegaTang::process reads the two return jacks at 0xf9f8 and 0xf9fc with no channel-count test anywhere, so patching only the left return leaves the right side of the mix without it. The left return's own line carries a clause saying so.

The mute does not reach the channel's own output. The gain used for output 0 at 0xf74c-0xf758 is the level alone; the mute is applied separately at 0xf798 on the path into the mix and the send. Anyone using the channel outputs as direct outs will find the mute buttons do nothing to them.

A channel leaves both the mix and the send as soon as its own output is patched: 0xf764, 0xf828, 0xf8e4 and 0xf99c read each output's channel count and skip that channel's contribution.

The expanders attach on the right. MegaTang::process reads rightExpander.module at +0x110 and compares its model against modelMTEX1 and modelMTEX2; MTEX1::process and MTEX2::process read leftExpander.module at +0xe8 and compare against modelMegaTang.

A debug printf was left in. When the module on the right is an MT-EX1, 0xf6c8-0xf6d0 calls printf with the format string "tang: C1 From: %.2f To: %.2f\n" on every sample, and MTEX1::process does the same with "ex1: C1 From: %.2f To: %.2f\n" at 0xc784. Neither affects the audio.

Parameter ranges: sends 0 to 1 with a default of 0, pans 0 to 1 with a default of 0.5 and a display multiplier of 200, levels 0 to 1 with a default of 1, all as percentages (0xe964 onward). The mutes are latching buttons; the byte a MuteButton sets on mouse-down (0x110f0) only drives a second lamp and is not in the audio path.

The four channel outputs are numbered so that index 0 is the jack the panel labels 1, which is the bottom one of that column; the tags follow the index, not the panel order.

MTEX1.notes:
MTEX1::process returns immediately unless leftExpander.module (+0xe8) has modelMegaTang as its model, so the module is completely inert anywhere except directly to the right of a MEGA-TANG. It has no outputs, which is why the census lists none.

All four knobs are configured 0 to 1 with a default of 0 and a display multiplier of 100 (0xc2cc onward).

lines: A copy of ALM's MFD: a stereo crossfader between two inputs, with a cue bus for listening to either of them on its own
Crossfades between the two inputs on an equal-power curve, A alone at one end and B alone at the other; it comes up in the middle, where both are passed at a reduced level
Routes the A input to the Cue outputs; what leaves the main outputs is not changed by it
Routes the B input to the Cue outputs; what leaves the main outputs is not changed by it
The left side of the A input
The left side of the B input
The right side of the A input; with nothing patched it takes the left side of A, so a mono source fills both
The right side of the B input; with nothing patched it takes the left side of B, so a mono source fills both
Moves the crossfade, adding to the knob, with the chosen voltage range covering the knob's whole travel; the total is clamped at each end
The left sides of A and B crossfaded together
The right sides of A and B crossfaded together
The left sides of whichever inputs are cued, added together
The right sides of whichever inputs are cued, added together
Note — the Cue outputs are silent until one of the two cue buttons is on. They ignore the crossfader entirely, which is what makes them useful for lining a track up before it is faded in.
Note — the crossfade comes up in the middle, where both inputs are passing at a reduced level rather than either one at full.
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Menu — Voltage Range: 10V, 5V — sets the voltage the X Fade CV input treats as a full sweep of the fader

MFD.notes:
The crossfade really is equal power, and the curve can be named exactly: MFD::process loads the double pi/2 at 0xa340 and calls cos twice, multiplying the A side by cos(x * pi/2) and the B side by cos((1 - x) * pi/2), where x is the fader position clamped to 0 and 1. ALM's page for the hardware says "Approx equal power crossfading", which agrees.

Both stereo inputs are mono-normalled: the right jack of each pair falls back to its own left jack (0xa3b8-0xa3e8), and the panel marks each left jack (m). This is the behaviour MEGA-TANG's return jacks print the same mark for and do not have.

The cue bus ignores the fader. 0xa2c8-0xa304 and 0xa3a0-0xa3f4 add the raw input voltages of whichever channels are cued, with no crossfade and no clamp.

The cue buttons are ALM BlueButtons with the momentary flag cleared in the constructor at 0xb554, so they hold their state rather than acting only while pressed. CueButton::onDragStart and onDragEnd (0xb778, 0xb7a4) set and clear a separate byte that drives a second lamp and is not read by the audio path. The lines avoid claiming either behaviour.

The X Fade CV is added to the knob and the total clamped, so negative voltage pulls the fader towards A and is not simply discarded, but it cannot pull it past A.

Nothing on this module is clamped to a voltage: only the fader position is.

lines: A copy of ALM's Stereo Sum: four stereo inputs summed into two stereo outputs, with the first pair feeding the second unless you use it
One of the two left signals added into the first pair of outputs
One of the two right signals added into the first pair of outputs
One of the two left signals added into the second pair of outputs
One of the two right signals added into the second pair of outputs
The first pair's two left signals added together; leaving this jack empty passes that sum on to the second pair's left output as well
The first pair's two right signals added together; leaving this jack empty passes that sum on to the second pair's right output as well
The second pair's two left signals added together, plus the first pair's left sum whenever the first left output is empty
The second pair's two right signals added together, plus the first pair's right sum whenever the first right output is empty
Note — with the upper outputs empty the module is one four-into-one stereo mixer. Patch them and it becomes two separate two-into-one mixers.
Note — the left and right sides break apart on their own. Patching only the upper left output takes the left side out of the cascade and leaves the right side joined.
Note — the module has no controls at all and nothing is clamped anywhere: it adds the voltages as they arrive.
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.

StereoSum.notes:
The cascade breaks per side, not per section. StereoSum::process reads output 0's channel count at 0x16670 and output 1's at 0x166b4, independently, so patching one of the upper outputs splits that side alone and leaves the other side of the stereo pair joined. Nothing on the panel shows this.

The module has no parameters at all, no lights and no context menu; process is 34 instructions of adds and two conditional selects.

The panel prints L and R over each input pair, a small circle over the first output pair and a small dot over the second, which is how the two halves are told apart.
